source: DBE Revised National Teaching Plans (Annual Teaching Plans), English Home Language, Foundation Phase. Week-by-week content and SBA tasks as published; used to align CAPS DI plans to the week of the term.
focusTime: Reading and Writing Focus Time (about 1 hour): Shared Reading then Shared Writing (about 15 minutes); word and sentence level work such as phonics, linked to the shared text (about 10 minutes); then Group Guided Reading with learners in reading-ability groups (2 groups a day, 15 minutes each). Paired and independent reading and independent writing happen outside the focus time.
principles: Content is scaffolded across weeks and repeated, so learners who miss days are not disadvantaged.
Assessment only on content taught, after learners have had time to practise.
Formative assessment is continuous and integrated into daily lessons; baseline assessment is informal, mostly oral and by observation.

baseline.note: Weeks 1–3: readiness programme with some Grade R content; informal readiness assessment in weeks 2–3, mostly by observation and orally.

Model the five finger strategy where each finger represents a strategy the reader can use to systematically work out how to read an unknown word and its meaning. The following information is taken from The Teacher's Handbook: Teaching Reading in the Early Grades (January 2008), Department of Education 1. Thumb: Leave the word out and read to the end of the sentence 2. First Finger: Look at the pictures and the heading 3. Second Finger: Ask yourself if there are any parts of the word that you recognize 4. Ring Finger: Sound the word out 5. Little Finger: Ask your teacher what the word means
